Definition: from G4649; to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard:--consider, take heed, look at (on), mark. Compare G3700.
BiblicalUsage: Skopeo means to look at, to take aim, to mark, and Paul uses it for what we look at and whom we watch. We look not at the things which are seen but at the things which are not seen, we take heed that the light in us be not darkness, we look on the things of others and not only our own, and we mark those who cause divisions and avoid them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe what I look at is what I become. The things that are seen are temporal and the things that are not seen are eternal, and I hold that my eyes must learn to love the unseen.
